Footnote 1 -- The investment is an IRA, over which I have no control, except for withdrawals.  Dividends, including long and short term gains, did not give rise to

 me quarterly and for year end.
 On January 16, 2020, I redeemed ("J") and, under the CARES Act, recontributed the same funds on August 11, 2020.  No gain or loss was recognized.
Footnote 2 -- The investment is an IRA, composed of managed investment companies disclosed in Lines 5 - 12 over which I have no control, except for
 withdrawals and transfers to and from other managed funds.  The Trustee does not sub-categorize gains and losses into dividends or short or long term gains or
 losses (see next paragraph).   
 One America Retirement Services, LLC, Adminstrator of the SSL Retirement Trust for Partners, and quarterly reports they provide, are the sources of the
 information provided in Part VII, Lines 5-12  I am one of the beneficiaries of the Trust.  One America advises that dividends received by the managed funds are
 not ascertainable.  One America states it administers five Stroock retirement plans, that money is co-mingled for all invested in the portfolio, that dividends and
 gains and losses are cumulated and are not posted at the participant level, and that "there is no way... to calculate [my] portion" of dividends.  My percentage of
 the whole is reported as a net total amount, for each managed fund and as a total for all managed funds, inclusive of all realizations by each managed fund for all
 securities managed by that fund.  The Stroock & Stroock & Lavan accounting department advises that they have no further information.  
Footnote 3 -- Cash value and dividends are applied to premiums, contributing to premiums payable on second to die life insurance.  Hence, the policy does not pay
 dividends.
Footnote 4 --On February 26, 2020, I redeemed ("N"), made up: from Dreyfus ("M"), Macquarie ("K") and Atlanta ("J").  On April 4, 2020, under the CARES Act,
 I recontributed the total amount of the redemption to Dreyfus ("N") as roll-overs.  Since the amounts redeemed were recontributed, no gain or loss was realized..

Re:

Dear Judge McKinley:

I respond to your letter of September 18, 2013.

1 do not know, and | am not able to identify, “cach stock, fund, or asset” managed

by the investment management companies identified in Lines 5 through 13 of Part VII of my

Financial Disclosure Report as of December 31, 2012.

The investment management companies identified on those lines function as

mutual funds, pooling funds contributed from many different sources. The funds contributed by

beneficiaries of the S&S&L Retirement Trust are overseen by trustees. The trustees are partners

of Stroock & Stroock & Lavan, LLP, the law firm from which I retired when I was appointed

United States District Judge in 1998. The trustees, in their choices of investment managers to

manage the funds contributed by the Trust, act on advice from professional investment advisors.

The investment managers chosen by the trustees invest the funds contributed, as

IRA and 401-K retirement funds, by the active and retired partners of the law firm and by the

firm's employees. The assets of the plans maintained by the firm are aggregated in a group trust

and are invested in mutual funds, exchange traded funds, and managed separate accounts in

accordance with a participant's direction. My funds are a small part of those funds and are

pooled with those funds.

1 do not have any say as to investment decisions made by any of the

managers. My only say is, periodically, to order transfer of funds allocable to me, totally or

partially, from one managed fund to another, but only among the several permitted by the Trust,

or to redeem funds as, for example, redemptions required by the Internal Revenue Code after the

age of 70 and a half.
